- We can't move to a full annualized commit immediately (need to align to our fiscal cadence).

2) Can the uplift be staged (e.g., 20% month 1, 40% month 2+) and then co-term or annualize later without backbilling?
3) Any options for crediting excess spend back at renewal if we convert to a larger commit?

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear context. We can support your timeline and have two pragmatic paths that match the constraints you outlined. Attached is a short pricing workbook with scenarios (helix_pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx).

Option A — Staged uplift with temporary surcharge (fastest to implement)
- Staged capacity increase: 20% in week 1, 40% from week 3 onward.
- Temporary surcharge: +15% on token/unit rates for the first 60–90 days to cover burst provisioning and priority capacity.
- No backbilling: if you annualize the uplift within 90 days, we credit surcharge differential back as a one-time account credit (applied at renewal) up to the amount invoiced under surcharge.

Option B — Bridge credit + amendment (procurement-friendly)
- We provision uplift at standard rate but invoice an upfront bridge (one-time invoice) to reserve capacity.
- If account converts to a higher commit at renewal, we apply the bridge as a credit toward the commitment (smooths finance treatment).

Key notes:
- Both paths support co-terming to your renewal — we can include a simple amendment (no model swaps).
- Legal can review a two-page amendment; Ben has a template we typically use.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-min call Tues 7/20 to pick path and confirm invoice/PO flow.
2) I'll share the amendment draft and the pricing workbook (attached).

Are you available Tue 7/20 10:00–11:00 PT or 14:00–15:00 PT?

Best,

Looping in a quick finance/ops perspective. Hi Samir — two pragmatic clarifications from our side:

1) If procurement needs clean invoice/PO flow, Option B (bridge credit) tends to be easiest for customers who cannot post a long-term commit immediately. We issue a one-time invoice for the bridge and attach it to the amendment; at renewal we apply as a credit against the larger commit.

2) For customers who prefer to avoid any surcharge on invoices, we can provide a reduced-surcharge variant (8–10%) if customer signs the amendment and provides the PO within 14 days of uplift go-live.

I've sketched the amendment language in the draft attached (amendment_draft_HLX.pdf) — it contains:
- Scope of uplift (units & effective date)
- Billing mechanics (bridge vs surcharge)
- Credit application at renewal and co-terming language

If you'd like, I can convert this to a DocuSign envelope once Samir confirms the path and PO number.
